newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hurt Bangladeshi worker dumped in Singapore ditch.
newsitem.headline: Hurt Bangladeshi worker dumped in Singapore ditch.

text.p: An illegal Bangladeshi worker injured at a Singapore construction site was dumped in a drainage ditch instead of being taken to hospital, police said on Friday.
In the first report of the case, they said one man had been arrested and another was being sought over the incident which left Mohammed Bashar, 24, paralysed from the waist down.
Bashar told Singapore's The New Paper he was hurt when a descending lift struck him on the head at a construction site in December. Bashar has been in hospital ever since.

Instead of being taken to hospital, two men tossed him in the ditch where he lay writhing in pain for two hours until he managed to attract the attention of a passing army jeep and soldiers rescued him.
"One man has been arrested and we are looking for another man. The person has been charged with a rash act endangering a human life," a police spokesman told Reuters.
Bashar told The New Paper he did not want to return home to Bangladesh.
"My family doesn't know I am paralysed. I don't want to break their hearts," he was quoted as saying on Friday.
He also said he had paid an agent in Bangladesh S$6,000 (US$4,200) for a Singapore work permit which turned out to be forged.
Singapore deports illegal workers but police said no decision had yet been made on whether to send him home.
